incumbent_revision_and_binary_hash.runtime: local installed Sage 10.10.rc0; incumbent loaded from immutable source snapshot

hypothesis_and_mechanism: Move prepared binary batch addition into Cython/NTL, reusing native GF2E scratch objects and prefix products instead of allocating Python finite-field elements for every intermediate. Preserve output construction and Python fallback for non-NTL fields.
predicted_complete_component_gain: A 25% reduction in the profiled 51.8% arithmetic share predicts ~1.15x component speed; a 2% complete gain needs ~3.8% reduction in that share. Profile is diagnostic, not a timing gate.
mathematical_invariants: exact Sage sums and point types/parents
infinity, inverse, doubling and order-two handling
one inversion and 3*(n-1) products for n active denominators
validate all inputs, retain non-NTL fallback
internal_counters_intentionally_changed: Python intermediate object allocation and NTL context restore counts
edge_cases_modes_and_architectures: generators that change active NTL context
construction_reset_cleanup_and_verificat: Primary warm API time includes pair creation where applicable, validation, native allocation, full point construction, exact equality to precomputed scalar Sage reference, and output destruction. Common field/fixture/scalar-reference setup recorded separately. Startup/import and compile excluded. CPU measured alongside wall time. Separate fresh-worker maximum-size RSS comparison includes identical setup. Profile separately after timings.
criteria_version: sage-native-addition-v1: local component criteria adapted from GNFS v1, because this is a mathematical arithmetic API rather than LAS; RSS measured in separate fresh workers, timing processes fresh per cell with balanced paired rounds.
rounds_and_order: 12 paired rounds per cell, 6 AB and 6 BA shuffled deterministically; one fresh process per cell; 4 complete calls per sample. Confirmation sources frozen before execution.
